How does usage work?
Each paid plan comes with a usage allowance that refreshes automatically on a daily and weekly basis. For the majority of users, this quota will be enough to fully cover all agent usage. Cost per message varies based on the model used, the task size and complexity, and the reasoning required.

Devin has four self-serve plans you can sign up for directly at app.devin.ai. For authoritative pricing, see the Devin pricing page. This page explains how the plans relate to each other and how billing mechanics work.

The Pro and Max plans are individual plans. They cannot be shared across multiple users. If you want multiple people to use Devin under a single subscription, you need the Teams plan.
The Jira and Microsoft Teams integrations are available on Enterprise only. To add them, contact sales.
Free
The Free plan lets you try Devin with limited usage. It includes:
Limited Devin usage
Access to Devin Review
Access to DeepWiki
Free users can upgrade to any paid plan at any time from Settings > Plans.
Pro
Pro is Devin’s entry-level individual plan. It’s designed for a single developer who uses Devin regularly. Pro includes:
A daily and weekly usage quota that covers Devin sessions, Devin CLI, and Devin Desktop
Pay-as-you-go on-demand credits for usage past your quota
Slack, Linear, and MCP integrations
Pro is a single-user plan. Pro subscribers cannot invite additional members to their organization. To work with teammates on a shared subscription, use the Teams plan.
Max
Max is for individual users who consistently exceed the Pro quota. It includes everything in Pro, plus a significantly larger weekly usage quota (with no daily cap), also shared between Devin sessions, Devin CLI, and Devin Desktop.
Like Pro, Max is a single-user plan and does not support multiple members.
Teams
The Teams plan is Devin’s self-serve plan for teams working with Devin together. Key properties:
$80/month: every Teams subscription is a flat $80/month, charged as prepaid on-demand credits.
On-demand credits are shared across the whole team. Every member draws from the same pool, and admins can top up at any time.
Every member gets the same access to Devin cloud sessions, Devin CLI, and Devin Desktop.
SAML or OIDC single sign-on for your team account. See SSO for Teams.
Cost controls with 3 usage tiers to cap how much each member can use. See Cost controls.
Free mode: each member can run up to 2 cloud sessions at a time at no cost. See Free mode.
Larger teams that need more controls should contact sales about Enterprise.
SSO
Teams admins can connect a SAML 2.0 or OIDC identity provider (Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, or any compliant IdP) from Settings > Authentication. On a Teams account, SSO signs in existing members only, so invite people before they sign in through SSO. Follow the identity provider setup steps in the SSO onboarding guide; its auto-membership, role assignment, and SCIM provisioning steps apply to Enterprise only.
Cost controls
Teams admins can cap each member’s usage with up to 3 usage tiers from Settings > Usage policies. Each tier sets a usage limit, members are assigned to a tier or fall back to the default tier, and new work is blocked once a member reaches their limit. The usage tiers section of the Usage policies guide explains how tiers work; budgets and budget-scoped limits apply to Enterprise only.
Free mode
On the Teams plan, every member can pick Free (powered by SWE-2) in the agent selector to run Devin cloud sessions at no cost. Each member can run up to 2 Free sessions at a time; to start a third, wait for one to finish or pick another mode. Sessions in other modes are billed as usual.
How quotas work
Pro and Max include a usage allowance that refreshes automatically on a calendar basis:
Pro has a daily and weekly allowance. The daily allowance is more than 1/7 of the weekly, so you can keep working through weekends without giving up overall capacity for the week.
Max has a weekly allowance only, with no daily cap.
Teams has no per-member allowance: all usage draws from the team’s shared on-demand credits.
When you’ve used up your allowance, on-demand credits keep you working without interruption. If your on-demand balance is also empty, sessions pause until your allowance refreshes or you purchase more credits.
If you have an eligible ChatGPT Go, Plus, or Pro subscription, you can also use your ChatGPT plan to pay for GPT model usage so it doesn’t count against your Devin allowance.
On-demand credits
On-demand credits are prepaid usage credit that fund any work past your plan’s included quota:
Roll over month-to-month. Purchased credits never expire.
Can be topped up at any time: select Purchase on-demand usage on the current plan card in Settings > Plans or Settings > Usage & limits. Select Configure auto-reload settings next to it to refill credits automatically.
Admins can set auto-reload thresholds and default session spending limits from Settings > Usage & limits.
On the Teams plan, credits are shared across all members, with no per-member balance. Any teammate can draw from the shared pool.
On the Teams plan, credits fund all usage, and the $80/month subscription is added to the pool as credits each month.
Devin Review and Automations Pricing
Automations and Devin Review are available on self-serve plans.

FAQ - MiniMax API Docs
Documentation Index
Fetch the complete documentation index at: /docs/llms.txt
Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.
Skip to main content
Which M Plan tiers are available?
The available subscription tiers are Go, Explore, and Build.
Tier Intended usage Usage quota relative to Go
Go Getting started 1×
Explore Everyday use 3×
Build Intensive use 7.5×
Which models does M Plan include? How do I switch models?
All three tiers support the M3.1 Flash text model, the H3 Image model, and the speech model, along with web search and multimodal understanding. Explore and Build also support the H3 video model.
To switch models, enter the model ID in your API request or tool configuration.
Do I need a separate subscription or M Plan API key to use MiniMax Code?
No. After subscribing to M Plan, sign in to MiniMax Code to get your subscription benefits. No separate subscription or M Plan API key is needed. For other AI tools, use your M Plan API key or sign in with MiniMax where supported.
Can I use my subscription in multiple tools at the same time?
Yes. You can use the same subscription in all supported tools, but usage is shared. Usage from all tools counts toward the same M Plan usage limits.
Is annual billing cheaper?
Yes. With annual billing, you pay for 10 months and get 2 months free.
Do text, speech, video, and image models have separate usage limits?
No. All models included in M Plan share the same weekly quota, which you can use however you need. Image and video models are subject only to the weekly window, not the 5-hour window; text, speech, and other models are also subject to the 5-hour window.
Do different models use my quota at the same rate?
No. How much of your quota each request uses depends mainly on:
Model: Models use your quota at different rates. Video generation uses more of your quota than text generation, so frequent video use can exhaust it faster.
Context length: Longer conversations and more files or code in context mean more content to process in each request.
Task complexity: Multi-step agent tasks send many requests in a row and call tools, so they use more of your quota than a single question and answer.
Reasoning effort: Higher reasoning effort can increase response time and usage.
If you are reaching your usage limit quickly, use lower reasoning effort for simple tasks, start new sessions when appropriate, and include only the files the task needs.
How can I check M Plan usage?
You can check M Plan usage in three ways:
Method 1: Visit the usage page
Visit the usage page to view your plan, usage limits, Credits, and usage history.
Method 2: Use MiniMax CLI
mmx quota
Method 3: Use the API endpoint
curl --location 'https://www.minimax.io/v1/token_plan/remains' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer <M Plan API key>' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json'
How is usage reset?
M Plan usage is shown through the console usage bar and controlled by usage windows:
Image and video models: Subject only to a weekly window, with no 5-hour window.
Text, speech, and other models: Subject to a 5-hour window and a weekly window.
Subscription cycle: Unused M Plan quota does not carry over to the next billing cycle.
Credits: Valid for one year from the date of purchase. This validity period is not reset when usage windows reset.
Both windows start with your first use: the 5-hour window lasts 5 hours, and the weekly window lasts 7 days. When a window ends, your full usage quota becomes available again, and your next use starts a new window. The two windows reset independently, so a 5-hour reset does not reset your weekly usage.
Does unused quota carry over?
No. Unused quota does not carry over to the next usage window or billing period.
What happens when I reach my usage limit?
When you reach your 5-hour or weekly limit, you can:
Use Credits: Your included M Plan quota is used first. Once you reach your limit, additional usage is deducted from your Credits by default, starting with the Credits that expire soonest. Credits apply only to the models and capabilities they support. You can also continue generating images with available Credits after reaching your weekly quota.
Upgrade to a higher tier: In MiniMax Code, click Upgrade in Settings > Usage & Models, or go to Plan Details and click Change plan to choose a higher tier with higher usage limits.
Wait for the usage window to reset: Image and video models are subject only to the weekly window; a 5-hour window reset does not reset their weekly usage. Text, speech, and other models are subject to 5-hour and weekly windows.
Switch to pay-as-you-go: Replace the M Plan API key in your tool with a standard API Key. Actual resource usage is charged to your account balance.
Will my account balance be charged when I reach my usage limit?
No. An M Plan API key uses your included M Plan quota and Credits. When you reach your usage limit, any remaining Credits are used next. Your account balance is charged only when you use a pay-as-you-go API Key.
What are the limits of M Plan? Is it suitable for production?
M Plan is designed for individual, interactive developer use, with higher tiers offering higher usage limits. Pay-as-you-go is recommended for production use.
Key limits include:
Rate limits (RPM / TPM): Requests may be throttled when exceeded, typically recovering within about one minute. Limits may tighten during peak traffic.
Image and video model usage: Subject only to a weekly window, with no 5-hour window.
Text, speech, and other model usage: Subject to 5-hour and weekly windows.
What are the platform traffic rules?
MiniMax may adjust request limits based on account usage and demand, including during peak hours, to keep the service available to all users.
What is an M Plan API key?
An M Plan API key is used for M Plan subscriptions and Credits. Configure it in AI agents and coding tools to call available models and capabilities.
M Plan API keys are separate from standard pay-as-you-go API Keys and cannot be used interchangeably.
Where do I get my M Plan API key?
After subscribing to M Plan, find your M Plan API key in Plan Details. Keep it secure; do not share it or commit it to a code repository.
Which tools can I use my M Plan API key with?
Any AI tool that supports the OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic-compatible protocol, such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Hermes Agent, and OpenClaw. See each tool’s guide for setup, or Other tools for general settings.
Can the M Plan API key and the standard API Key be used interchangeably?
No.
M Plan API key: Uses your included M Plan quota and Credits. API endpoints with pay-as-you-go pricing deduct from your included M Plan quota at the corresponding endpoint price. Credits can be used for the models and capabilities they support and can cover eligible overflow beyond subscription usage limits.
Standard API Key: Uses pay-as-you-go billing for API Platform endpoints. Actual resource usage consumes your account balance.
Why is my account balance still being charged after subscribing?
Usually because the tool is using a pay-as-you-go API Key. Pay-as-you-go API Keys charge your account balance and do not use your M Plan usage. Replace it with your M Plan API key.
Which models do Credits support?
Credits support text, video, image, and speech models, along with web search and multimodal understanding.
How are Credits valued and charged?
Credits can be used for supported models and capabilities. You can use them on their own or after reaching your M Plan usage limit.
Calls to models with pay-as-you-go pricing deduct the equivalent Credits amount at the model’s API price.
When both your included M Plan quota and Credits can cover a request, your included quota is used first, followed by Credits for the excess.
Validity: Credits are valid for one year from the date of purchase.
How long are Credits valid?
Credits are valid for one year from the date of purchase. Their validity is not reset when usage windows reset.
Can I use Credits without an M Plan subscription?
Yes. Credits can be purchased separately and used without an M Plan subscription.
Note:
If you also subscribe to M Plan, your included M Plan quota is used before your Credits.
In MiniMax Code, Credits purchased on their own do not include M Plan subscription benefits, such as additional cloud projects, scheduled tasks, and website publishing limits, custom domains, and watermark removal.
For resources outside M Plan coverage, use a pay-as-you-go API Key.
How do I upgrade, and when does it take effect?
In Plan Details, click Change plan and choose your target tier. The unused portion of your current subscription is prorated by the time remaining and applied toward the upgrade, so you only pay the difference. Once you complete payment, the upgrade takes effect immediately, and your subscription then renews at the new tier’s price. See Upgrades and cancellation.
Can I downgrade?
Downgrades are not currently supported.
Can I switch from monthly to annual billing?
A monthly subscription can be upgraded to a higher tier with monthly or annual billing. An annual subscription can be upgraded to a higher tier with annual billing.
How do I turn off auto-renewal?
Turn off auto-renewal in Plan Details. Your benefits remain available for the current paid period, and the subscription will not renew when it ends.
If you change your mind, you can turn auto-renewal back on in Plan Details before your subscription expires.
What do I need to do as a Token Plan subscriber?
Nothing. Your current plan and benefits stay the same, and as long as auto-renewal stays on, your subscription renews at the original price with the same benefits. You can also upgrade to M Plan at any time, and the unused portion of your current subscription will be credited toward the cost. Learn more about what changes for Token Plan subscribers.
How is TPS (Tokens Per Second) calculated for LLMs?
TPS measures the number of tokens generated per second, and is used to evaluate the inference output speed of a model. The formula is:
TPS=Number of output tokensTime of last token−Time of first token\text{TPS} = \frac{\text{Number of output tokens}}{\text{Time of last token} - \text{Time of first token}}TPS=Time of last token−Time of first tokenNumber of output tokens​
In other words, timing starts when the model outputs the first token and ends when the last token is generated. The total number of tokens produced is then divided by that elapsed time (in seconds).
TPS may fluctuate during actual usage. The TPS values indicated on each model page are reference values.
Still getting 401 after login?
mmx auth login usually auto-detects the service region from your API Key. If you still get 401, region detection likely failed. Set it manually:
mmx config set --key region --value global # Global API Key
mmx config set --key region --value cn # Mainland China API Key
Run mmx auth status to confirm the active region matches the platform your key comes from.

现在有哪些 M Plan 套餐可以选择？
当前订阅档位为 Go、Explore 和 Build。
档位 使用定位 额度（相对 Go）
Go 轻松上手 1 倍（基准）
Explore 日常主力 3 倍
Build 高强使用 12 倍
M Plan 包含哪些模型？如何切换模型？
三个档位均支持文本模型 M3.1 Flash、图片模型 H3 Image、声音模型，以及网络搜索和多模态理解能力。Explore 和 Build 额外支持视频模型 H3。
如需切换模型，在 API 请求或工具配置中填写对应的模型 ID 即可。
在 MiniMax Code 中使用，需要单独订阅或配置 API Key 吗？
不需要。订阅 M Plan 后，登录 MiniMax Code 即可享有会员权益，无需另行订阅，也无需配置订阅 Key。只有在 Claude Code、Cursor 等其他 AI 工具中使用时，才需要配置订阅 Key。
是否可以同时在多个工具中使用我的订阅套餐？
可以，您可以在所有支持的工具中使用同一订阅套餐，但额度是共享的，所有工具的使用会消耗同一套餐额度。
年付是否更优惠？
是的，年付只需支付 10 个月的费用，相当于省下 2 个月。
文本、声音、视频和图片的额度是分开的吗？
不是。M Plan 包含的所有模型共用同一份周额度，您可以根据需要灵活使用。图片和视频模型仅受周窗口限制，不受 5 小时窗口限制；文本、声音等模型还受 5 小时窗口限制。
不同模型的额度消耗一样吗？
不一样。每次使用消耗多少额度，主要取决于以下几点：
模型：不同模型的消耗不同，其中视频生成的消耗远高于文本对话，经常生成视频时额度会用得更快。
上下文长度：对话越长、读入的文件和代码越多，每次请求需要处理的内容就越多。
任务复杂度：多步骤的 Agent 任务会连续发起多次请求并调用工具，消耗明显高于单次问答。
思考深度：文本模型的思考深度越高，生成的思考内容越多，消耗也越多。
如果额度消耗较快，可以为简单任务选择较低的思考深度，适时开启新会话，并只引入完成任务所需的文件。
如何查看 M Plan 用量？
您可以通过以下三种方式查看 M Plan 用量：
方式一：访问套餐用量页面
访问 套餐用量 页面查看您的套餐、额度、积分和用量情况。
方式二：使用 MiniMax CLI
mmx quota
方式三：使用 API 接口查询
curl --location 'https://www.minimax.cn/v1/token_plan/remains' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer <API Key>' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json'
用量是如何重置的？
M Plan 用量通过控制台用量进度条展示，并受额度窗口控制：
图片和视频模型：仅受周窗口控制，不受 5 小时窗口限制。
文本、声音等模型：受 5 小时窗口和周窗口控制。
订阅周期：未使用完的套餐内 M Plan 额度不会结转到下一个计费周期。
积分包：自购买之日起 1 年内有效，不会因为套餐窗口刷新而重置有效期。
两个窗口都从首次使用时开始计时，5 小时窗口持续 5 小时，周窗口持续 7 天。窗口结束后，额度恢复到所在档位的上限，下一次使用时开启新窗口。两个窗口各自独立刷新，5 小时窗口刷新不会恢复本周已用的额度。
没用完的额度会累积或结转吗？
不会。未用完的额度不会累积到下一个窗口，也不会结转到下一个计费周期。
额度用完后怎么办？
达到 5 小时或周额度上限后，您可以选择：
使用积分包：扣费顺序为 M Plan 额度优先、积分包其次。达到上限后，超出的用量默认从积分包中扣除积分，按到期时间先后扣除。积分包仅用于其支持的模型与能力；图片模型的周额度用尽后，也可使用可用的积分包继续生成图片。
升级订阅套餐：在 MiniMax Code 的「设置 > 用量与模型」中点击「升级」，或在 套餐详情 页面点击 管理订阅，选择更高档位以获得更高的额度。
等待额度窗口重置：图片和视频模型仅受周窗口控制，等待 5 小时窗口刷新不会恢复其周额度；文本、声音等模型受 5 小时窗口和周窗口控制。
切换到按量付费：将工具中的订阅 Key 更换为普通开放平台 API Key，按资源实际使用量消耗账户余额。
额度用完后，会自动扣账户余额吗？
不会。订阅 Key 只使用 M Plan 额度和积分包。额度用完后，如有积分包剩余，会继续扣除。账户余额只有在使用按量计费 API Key 时才会扣除。
M Plan 有哪些使用限制？是否适合生产环境？
M Plan 面向个人开发者的交互式使用场景，更高的套餐等级提供更高的额度上限。生产环境建议使用按量付费。
主要限制包括：
速率限制（RPM / TPM）：超出后会限流，通常约 1 分钟恢复，高峰期可能动态收紧。
图片和视频模型额度：仅受周窗口控制，不受 5 小时窗口限制。
文本、声音等模型额度：受 5 小时窗口和周窗口控制。
平台流量规则是什么？
为保障对所有用户的服务稳定性和可用性，MiniMax 平台可能在高峰时段实施动态限流策略。
为了避免少数异常流量挤占公共算力池，并保障大多数用户的稳定体验，平台会基于账户使用维度进行速率调控。同时，我们正在持续推进算力扩容与系统优化，努力提供更稳定、可靠的服务。
订阅 Key 是什么？
订阅 Key 是用于 M Plan 订阅套餐和积分包的 Key。您可以将它配置到 AI Agent 和编程工具中，调用可用的模型与能力。
订阅 Key 与普通按量计费 API Key 相互独立，不能混用。
在哪里获取订阅 Key？
订阅 M Plan 后，在 套餐详情 中查看您的订阅 Key。请妥善保管，不要泄露给他人或提交到代码仓库。
订阅 Key 可以在哪些工具中使用？
支持 OpenAI 兼容或 Anthropic 兼容协议的 AI 工具都可以使用，例如 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、OpenCode、Hermes Agent 和 OpenClaw，配置方法见各工具的接入教程。其他工具可参考 其他工具 中的通用配置。
M Plan 的订阅 Key 和开放平台普通的 API Key 可以混用吗？
不可以。
订阅 Key：用于 M Plan 套餐内额度和积分包。已有按量计费价格的 API 端点会按对应按量计费价格扣减套餐内 M Plan 额度。积分包可用于其支持的模型与能力，并承接订阅额度之外的合规超额用量。
普通开放平台 API Key：用于按量计费访问开放平台 API 接口，按资源实际使用量计费，消耗您的账户余额。
为什么订阅后仍在扣账户余额？
通常是因为工具中填写的是按量计费 API Key。按量计费 API Key 会扣除账户余额，不会使用 M Plan 额度。请将工具中的 Key 更换为 订阅 Key。
积分包支持哪些模型？
积分包支持文本、视频、图片和声音模型，以及网络搜索和多模态理解能力。
积分包怎么折算？
积分包可用于其支持的模型与能力，既可单独使用，也可在 M Plan 套餐内额度用尽后继续使用。
使用积分包调用已有按量计费价格的模型时，会按该模型的 API 价格折算为积分扣减。
如果同一用量同时可由套餐内额度和积分包覆盖，系统会优先扣除套餐内额度，超出部分再扣除积分包中的积分。
有效期：积分自购买之日起 1 年内有效。
积分包的有效期是多久？
积分包自购买之日起 1 年内有效，不会因套餐额度窗口刷新而重置有效期。
没有 M Plan 订阅也可以使用积分包吗？
可以。积分包可以单独购买，没有 M Plan 订阅也能使用。
需要注意：
如同时订阅了 M Plan，会先扣除套餐内额度，再扣除积分包。
在 MiniMax Code 中，单独购买积分包不享有 M Plan 会员权益，例如更多的云端项目、定时任务和网站发布额度，以及自定义域名、移除网站水印等。
如需使用 M Plan 覆盖范围之外的资源，请使用按量计费 API Key。
如何升级套餐？什么时候生效？
进入 套餐详情，点击 管理订阅 并选择目标档位。当前订阅未使用的部分会按剩余时间折算抵扣，您只需支付差额。完成付款后，升级立即生效，之后按新档位的价格续费。详见 升级与取消。
可以降级吗？
暂不支持降级。
可以从月付改为年付吗？
月付订阅可以升级为更高档位的月付或年付；年付订阅可以升级为更高档位的年付。
如何取消自动续订？
您可以在 套餐详情 中关闭自动续费。关闭后，当前周期内的权益照常可用，到期后不再续费。
自动续费关闭后无法恢复。如需继续订阅，请重新购买套餐；如果在当前订阅到期前升级，剩余价值可以抵扣费用。
我是 Token Plan 用户，需要做什么？
无需任何操作，当前套餐与权益保持不变；只要自动续费保持开启，就会按原价格和原有权益续费。您也可以随时升级到 M Plan，当前订阅未使用的部分会折算抵扣，具体安排见 Token Plan 老用户说明。
开票金额怎么计算？
可开票金额以订单实际支付的金额为准：
付款方式 可开票金额
支付宝 支付宝实际支付的金额
账户余额 余额实际扣除的金额
支付宝与余额组合 两种方式实际支付金额的合计
使用代金券 扣除代金券后实际支付的金额，代金券抵扣部分不可开票
升级订阅 实际补付的差额，原订阅抵扣部分不可开票
语言模型的 TPS（Tokens Per Second）是如何计算的？
TPS 表示模型每秒生成的 token 数量，用于衡量模型的推理输出速度。计算公式为：
TPS=输出 token 数量最后一个 token 的生成时间−第一个 token 的生成时间\text{TPS} = \frac{\text{输出 token 数量}}{\text{最后一个 token 的生成时间} - \text{第一个 token 的生成时间}}TPS=最后一个 token 的生成时间−第一个 token 的生成时间输出 token 数量​
即从模型输出第一个 token 开始计时，到最后一个 token 输出完成为止，期间生成的 token 总数除以这段时间（秒）。
TPS 在实际使用中可能存在波动，各页面上标注的 TPS 为参考值。
登录后仍报 401 怎么办？
通常 mmx auth login 会根据 API Key 自动检测服务区域（若购买的是国内套餐，在进行 mmx auth login 配置时尽量不要开 VPN）。若仍报 401，大概率是 region 未自动匹配成功，可手动指定：
mmx config set --key region --value cn # 国内 API Key
mmx config set --key region --value global # 海外 API Key
执行 mmx auth status 确认当前 region 与 Key 来源平台一致。

Kimi Coding Plan: Features, Models, and How to Get Started
Kimi Coding Plan Guide: Plans, Costs, And Setup
Looking for a coding plan that helps you build faster? Kimi Code gives you an AI coding agent for your terminal and IDE, with flexible plans and usage limits. Explore how a coding plan works, compare features and pricing, and start coding smarter today.
10 min read/Updated: 2026-11-19
Get coding plan
Managing AI coding tasks can become expensive and time-consuming, especially when you need reliable tools for everyday development. A coding plan offers a more structured way to access AI-powered coding assistance and streamline your workflow. Kimi Coding Plan provides developers with access to capable AI models and coding features designed to support programming tasks. This guide explores its key features, available models, benefits, and how to get started.
Kimi coding plan: Plans and pricing explained
Kimi Code is an AI coding agent that can understand project files, plan modifications, edit code, execute terminal commands, and review results. It helps developers handle complex, multi-step development tasks through compatible tools such as the Kimi Code CLI, VS Code, and a desktop application.
Kimi Code is included in eligible Kimi membership subscriptions rather than offered as a separate coding subscription. International users can access Kimi Code with the Plus, Pro, Max, and Ultra plans. Each tier provides different usage allowances and capabilities, allowing developers to select a subscription based on their coding frequency and project requirements. Unlike the pay-as-you-go Kimi API, Kimi Code access is covered by membership benefits and subject to the applicable usage limits. You can visit the official Kimi membership pricing page to review the latest plans and subscription details.
Item Plus Pro Max Ultra
Monthly billing $19/month $39/month $99/month $199/month
Annual billing (monthly equivalent) $15/month ($180/year) $31/month ($372/year) $79/month ($948/year) $159/month ($1,908/year)
Kimi Code access Included Included Included Included
Key benefits Access to Kimi Code and supported coding models Adds Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed access and higher usage allowances Larger usage allowances for demanding coding workflows Highest usage allowances for intensive development workflows
Annual subscriptions are charged upfront for the full year, with the monthly figures shown above representing the equivalent cost. Prices exclude applicable taxes and may vary by region or purchase conditions. Kimi Code usage is subject to membership-specific limits, so check the official pricing page for the latest details.
Get coding plan
How Kimi Code usage is calculated
Kimi Code usage is based on your membership's available credits and applicable rate limits. Kimi Code usage is subject to a rolling five-hour rate limit and draws credits from the shared monthly membership pool. Coding tasks consume credits from this pool, which is also used by other eligible Kimi services. This means that using other Kimi features can reduce the credits available for coding tasks.
If your included credits are insufficient, eligible members can enable Extra Usage to continue using Kimi Code with additional pay-as-you-go credits. These credits can also be shared across Kimi on the web and Kimi Code.
Actual consumption depends on factors such as the models used and the complexity of coding tasks. For a detailed explanation of usage calculation, rate limits, credit consumption, and Extra Usage, refer to the official Kimi Code membership documentation.
How to check and monitor Kimi Code usage
You can check your remaining credits and monitor usage through several interfaces:
Kimi Code CLI: Enter /usage in the CLI to view your current usage information.
Kimi Code Desktop: Open Settings to review usage and available credits.
Kimi web console: Visit the Kimi account or usage console to check your membership balance and consumption.
Regularly checking your usage helps you understand how quickly coding tasks consume credits and decide whether your current membership tier provides sufficient capacity for your development workload.
Explore the features of Kimi Code
Kimi Code combines AI-powered coding assistance with tools for planning, editing, and executing development tasks. Its features help developers manage existing codebases, handle complex changes, and improve their overall programming workflow through an AI coding plan.
AI-powered code generation and editing: Describe a feature, bug, or refactoring task in natural language. Kimi Code can generate code, fix errors, modify existing implementations, and improve code quality.
Codebase understanding: Read, search, and analyze project files to understand the code structure, dependencies, and relationships before making changes.
Plan mode for controlled development: Review the proposed implementation steps before execution. You can adjust the plan and approve the approach before Kimi Code modifies project files.
Goal mode for long-running tasks: Set a specific objective and let Kimi Code work through multiple steps toward completion. You can pause, resume, or cancel the task whenever needed.
Terminal execution and verification: Run commands, scripts, builds, and tests directly on your computer. Review the output to identify errors and verify whether the changes work as expected.
Multi-agent collaboration: Delegate complex tasks to specialized agents that can handle different parts of a project. This supports parallel research, coding, and problem-solving.
Flexible development environments: Access Kimi Code through its desktop application, command-line interface (CLI), or supported IDE integrations. Choose the environment that best fits your development habits and switch between interfaces as your projects require.
Browser and visual assistance: Access web pages within the desktop environment and share page context with the Agent. You can also use screenshots and visual annotations to explain the changes you want.
Custom skills, plugins for extensibility: Extend coding workflows with reusable Skills, plugins, and MCP integrations. These options allow you to connect additional tools and add specialized capabilities to your development environment.
Get coding plan
How to choose the right Kimi coding plan
Choosing a Kimi coding plan depends on how often you code, the complexity of your projects, and the model capabilities you need. While all four eligible plans include Kimi Code, they differ in model access and available usage allowances. Consider the following scenarios when deciding which tier fits your development workflow.
Plus: For everyday coding and smaller projects: Plus is a practical starting point if you mainly use Kimi Code for code generation, debugging, code explanations, routine feature development, and edits across a limited number of files. It provides access to supported coding models without requiring a higher-tier subscription. However, it does not include the additional HighSpeed model access or 1M-token context capability available with Pro and above.
Pro: For larger codebases and more demanding development tasks: Pro is worth considering if you regularly work with multiple files, investigate complex dependencies, or refactor larger projects. It adds K3.1 Pro Highspeed access and unlocks the 1M-token context window, which can help Kimi Code process more project context within a single workflow. The HighSpeed option is also useful when faster model responses are a priority.
Max: For frequent coding with higher usage requirements: Max is more suitable if Kimi Code is part of your daily development workflow and you frequently handle longer sessions or complex, multi-step tasks. Its larger membership allowance provides more room for coding alongside other Kimi features. Consider this tier if you regularly approach the usage capacity of Pro.
Ultra: For intensive, high-volume development workflows: Ultra is designed for users who need the largest available membership allowance among the four tiers. It is worth considering if you use Kimi Code extensively throughout the day and also rely heavily on other Kimi services. The additional allowance can provide more flexibility for sustained development work.
Before upgrading, consider how much of your membership credit pool you allocate to coding versus other Kimi features. All membership services share the same monthly credit pool, so a higher tier may be more suitable if you regularly use Kimi Work, Deep Research, or other credit-consuming features alongside Kimi Code.
If you are unsure which plan to choose, starting with Plus or Pro and reviewing your actual usage is a practical approach. You can check consumption in the Kimi Code Console and use that information to decide whether a higher tier is necessary.
Kimi Code models: Which one should you choose
Kimi Code offers different AI models and inference options through eligible membership plans. Model availability depends on your subscription tier and the client or integration you use.
The latest flagship release is the Kimi K3, which brings improvements in coding, reasoning, and long-running agent workflows. The following table compares the available models and their recommended uses.
Model Availability and capabilities Recommended use
K3.1 Pro Available on Plus and above; up to 1M context on Pro and above; supports thinking mode Complex coding, large codebase analysis, and multi-file refactoring
K3.1 Pro Highspeed Available on Pro and above; approximately 2–3× the output speed of standard K3.1 Pro Faster execution of demanding coding tasks
K3 Available on Plus and above; up to 1M context on Pro and above Large-project analysis and long-context development
K3 256K Available on Plus and above; supports up to 256K context Routine coding, code completion, and smaller file edits
K2.8 Preview Available on Plus and above; supports up to 1M context General AI coding and agent workflows
K2.7 Code HighSpeed Available on Pro and above under the legacy model mapping Faster coding workflows using the previous coding model
Model availability may change as Kimi Code introduces new models or updates existing ones. For the latest model list, subscription requirements, and supported capabilities, refer to the official Kimi Code model documentation.
How to choose:
Choose K3.1 Pro for complex development tasks that require deeper reasoning and an understanding of project dependencies.
Choose K3.1 Pro Highspeed when faster output is a priority, and your subscription includes access.
Choose K3 or K3.1 Pro with a longer context window to analyze extensive repositories.
Choose K3 256K for routine coding tasks that do not require a larger context window.
Use K2.8 Preview as an alternative for general coding and agent workflows.
For developers, comparing the best AI coding plan, model access, context limits, and inference speed are important factors to consider alongside subscription costs.
Important: K3.1 Pro models require thinking to remain enabled and support configurable reasoning effort, with high as the default setting. For a more stable experience, start a new session when switching to the latest K3.1 Pro models instead of changing models within an existing session.
Get coding plan
What can you do with Kimi Code
Kimi Code supports a wide range of software development tasks, from understanding existing projects and generating code to debugging, refactoring, and working with external tools. Here are some common use cases:
Understand codebases and implement features: Kimi Code can analyze project structures, dependencies, and relationships between files to understand how an application works. It can then generate new code or modify existing implementations across multiple files, helping developers build frontend components, implement backend logic, integrate APIs, and update configurations. For example, you can ask it to add a password reset feature, including the frontend form, backend endpoint, and input validation. It can inspect the existing project and coordinate changes across the relevant files.

Which is deducted first, Extra Usage or subscription quota?
Time-limited quotas such as the subscription are deducted first; Extra Usage is only deducted as a fallback once all time-limited quotas are exhausted.
When I hit the monthly / weekly (legacy plans) / hourly limit, or get rate-limited mid-session, can I keep going?
Yes. Once Extra Usage is enabled you're not affected by subscription limits — whenever any quota is reached it seamlessly switches to the Extra Usage balance, so tasks don't stop or error out, and only Extra Usage is deducted without affecting your membership quota refresh.

Billing depends on the request's input/output volume and cache hit rate; Extra Usage pricing is close to the Kimi Open Platform's official API, and for heavy usage upgrading your subscription is usually more cost-effective.

Yes — it's credit-based, doesn't expire, and stacks; it stays usable after the subscription lapses, but you can't top up during the lapse and must re-subscribe to top up again.
When the balance is nearly used up (e.g. a 25 RMB top-up), will the current request finish?
It guarantees the "last model call" completes even if its billing exceeds the limit, but it doesn't guarantee the whole task will finish.

Not yet supported.

Visit the Kimi Membership page and follow the instructions to submit an invoice request or upgrade your plan.

How does Kiro pricing work?
How does Kiro pricing work?
Kiro offers flexible pricing tiers designed around how developers use Kiro. New users can start with the perpetual Kiro Free tier, which includes 50 credits per month. The Free Tier includes access to open weight models and Claude Sonnet 4.5, with limits. Plans for teams (of 2 and more) are available for $20/seat/month and come with 500 included credits per seat with an option to purchase credits at $0.04 per add-on credit. Which models does Kiro use under the hood?
Which models does Kiro use under the hood?
By default, your prompts are processed by Auto, an agent that uses a mix of different frontier models, combined with specialized models that are experts in specific tasks, intent detection, caching, and other techniques to give you a better balance of quality, latency, and costs. You can also choose a specific model, including OpenAI's GPT-5.6 (Sol, Terra, and Luna), Anthropic's Claude models (Opus 5.5, Opus 5, Sonnet 5.5, and Haiku 5.5), xAI's Grok 4.7, and open weight models such as Kimi K3, DeepSeek 3.2, MiniMax M2.5, GLM-5, and Qwen3 Coder Next. See the [models page](/docs/models) for the full list and current credit multipliers.
How does the free trial work?
How does the free trial work?
The first time you upgrade from Kiro Free to Pro, the rest of that month is free, and you get 500 trial credits to use within 12 months. Plan fees and credits are prorated to the second, so you get plan credits for the time left in the month, and your first bill arrives on the 1st of the following month. Trial credits are used after you run out of plan credits. Upgrading to a paid subscription requires a valid credit card. For example, if you upgrade to Pro ($20/month) at 00:00 UTC on the 15th of a 30-day month, 16 days remain: your prorated fee is $10.67, which the free month covers, so you pay $0 and get 533 plan credits plus 500 trial credits. If you start on Pro+, Pro Max, or Power instead, the free Pro month still counts, and you pay only the difference between your plan's prorated price and the prorated Pro price (for example, $10.67 for Pro+ in the same scenario). If you go back to Kiro Free, your unused trial credits carry over, but you can only spend them on free-tier models. The free trial applies only to your first upgrade. If you upgrade again later, your fee and credits are prorated as usual, without a free month. If you upgraded before November 1, you keep the $20 discount and your unused credits.
What is a credit?
What is a credit?
A credit is a unit of work in response to user prompts. Simple prompts can consume less than 1 credit. More complex prompts, such as executing a spec task, typically cost more than 1 credit. Additionally, different models consume credits at different rates, with a prompt executed via Sonnet 4.6 costing more credits than executing it with Auto. For example, a given task that consumes X credits to execute in Auto, will cost you 1.3X credits to execute via Sonnet 4.6. Credits are metered to the second decimal point, so the least number of credits a task can consume is 0.01 credits.
What can I use credits for?
What can I use credits for?
Any prompt you ask Kiro to execute, whether in vibe mode or spec mode, as well as spec refinement, task execution, and agent hook execution, will consume credits.
How can I track my credit usage?
How can I track my credit usage?
You can see the monthly credit limits for your plan, the number of credits used, and credits remaining in your subscription dashboard accessible in Kiro. Credit usage is updated at least every 5 minutes. For credit pooling, credit usage can be tracked via admin dashboards.
How do Kiro workflows affect credit usage?
How do Kiro workflows affect credit usage?

Prorated fee = (seconds remaining / total seconds in month) × monthly plan fee
Prorated credits = (seconds remaining / total seconds in month) × monthly plan credits
For example, Pro costs $20 per month with 1,000 credits. In a 30-day month (2,592,000 seconds), upgrading at 00:00 UTC on day 15 leaves 16 days (1,382,400 seconds). The prorated fee is (1,382,400 / 2,592,000) × $20 = $10.67, and the prorated credits are (1,382,400 / 2,592,000) × 1,000 = 533. If you upgrade later in the day, fewer seconds remain, so the prorated fee and credits are lower.

Starting on a bigger plan
You can make your first upgrade to Pro+, Pro Max, or Power instead of Pro. The free Pro month still counts toward it: you pay only the difference between your plan's prorated price and the prorated Pro price, and you receive that plan's prorated credits plus 500 trial credits.

Upgrading again
If you upgrade again later, Kiro prorates your fee and credits for the time left in the month. You don't get a second free month.
If you purchased add-on credits before upgrading, they remain in your balance. After the upgrade, Kiro uses your new plan's higher credit allocation first, so your add-on credits are preserved for future use rather than being consumed immediately.
Info
If you go back to the Kiro Free tier, your unused trial credits carry over. On the Free tier, you can spend them only on Free-tier models. Note that downgrades take effect in the following month and upgrades are effective immediately.
Downgrading
If you downgrade from a higher tier to a lower tier mid-month, you are charged the full fee for the current month. For example, if you downgrade from Pro+ to Pro on June 2nd, you'll be charged the full Pro+ subscription fee for June. From July onward, you will be charged the Pro fee.
Credit reset
For all tiers, your plan credits renew at the beginning of the next billing cycle. Trial credits don't reset at the end of the month. They stay available until they expire, 12 months after you receive them.

What happens when I reach the monthly limit of my plan?
Using up your plan credits is not the same as using up every credit in your balance. When your plan credits are exhausted, Kiro continues with the other credits you hold. If your first upgrade gave you trial credits, Kiro uses them after your plan credits; they stay available until they expire, 12 months after you receive them. Requests pause only when you have no credits left, until your plan credits reset at the start of the next month or you purchase add-on credits.
The Kiro Free tier has fixed monthly limits and doesn't support add-on credits. If you hit a Free limit, you can upgrade to a paid plan
for immediate additional capacity.
On paid plans, you can purchase add-on credits to continue working uninterrupted beyond your included limits. You can also upgrade
to a higher plan at any time. The upgrade takes effect immediately, with the fee and credits prorated for the time left in the month.
